folders.description: Wraps an existing OCI image as a Package. Use it through pkg_import with source oci://<registry>/<repository>@sha256:<digest>: it inspects the image in its registry and returns a manifest that runs that exact digest.

folders.description: Counts every span, log record and metric point kitbashd fans out, per member and in total, and reports the totals back as metrics. Run it to see whether Telemetry is flowing. Deliveries must carry the fan out secret kitbashd gives this Process.

content.text:
# Handbook

This machine runs kitbash. Everything you can see through this connection lives in two places.

- `/org` is shared. Every member reads it. Writes go through an approval by an admin.
- `/home/<you>` is yours. Write freely, it is a git repository and every write is a commit.

A folder is visible only when it carries a `kitbash.yaml` with a name and a description. When you create a folder, write its manifest first.

The logo next to this file is here so image reading can be verified.

item.text: I’m making a shared web app with saved links, optional custom names, and a copy button. Links will redirect from the server, so they’ll work for everyone in the group and survive restarts.

files.content:
name: little-link
description: Create persistent short links for study group resources.
deploy:
  units:
    - type: container
      build: .
      expose: http
      port: 8080
      mounts:
        - source: /home/bench-20260920-0100/link-shortener/data
          target: /data
          mode: rw

FROM python:3.12-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY server.py index.html test_server.py ./
RUN python -m unittest -v
EXPOSE 8080
CMD ["python", "server.py"]

↗ little link
Made for sharing
LESS LINK. MORE LEARNING.

Big ideas.
Little links.

Readings, notes, and everything in between.
Turn a long URL into something your study group can share.

Letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores. At least 3 characters.

READY TO SHARE

Your recent links

History stays in this browser. Anyone with a short link can open it.

A little less clutter in the group chat.

item.text: The app is running, and tests for saved links, duplicate names, and invalid URLs passed. I’m checking the live page and redirect behavior now.

item.command:
/bin/zsh -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import urllib.request, urllib.error, json
base='https://go.bench-20260920-0100.kitbash.zyx.tw'
assert urllib.request.urlopen(base).status == 200
req=urllib.request.Request(base+'/api/links',data=json.dumps({'url':'https://example.com/study?chapter=1'}).encode(),headers={'Content-Type':'application/json'})
r=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req)); print('Created:',r)
class NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
 def redirect_request(self,*args): return None
try: urllib.request.build_opener(NoRedirect).open(base+'/'+r['slug'])
except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
 assert e.code==302 and e.headers['Location']=='https://example.com/study?chapter=1'
 print('Redirect: 302 with exact destination; homepage: 200')
try: urllib.request.urlopen(base+'/does-not-exist-test')
except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
 assert e.code==404
 print('Missing link: 404')
PY"
